blocks.text: LINGAYEN, Pangasinan – By implementing programs and projects aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the Pangasinan provincial government raised its SDG score from 50 in 2019 to 89 in 2024, out of a targeted score of 102. This was the main finding of the Pangasinan SDGs Report, a study conducted by researchers from the Pangasinan Polytechnic College (PPC) under the SDGs Localization Research Project of the Center for Pangasinan Studies (CPS). READ: Philippines shows stronger progress in SDGs The study documented improvements in food and nutrition, health, education, environment, and finance and justice, said Professor Raymundo D.
